user_goal: Make every durable progress submission understandable to the user without forcing them to interpret manifest_version, controller revision, protocol version, or Git SHA, while preserving exact technical traceability and avoiding a new source of truth.
proposed_mechanism_from_user: Use a date-like or SVN-style sequence so revisions are easier to understand.
root_cause: Several valid technical version namespaces are exposed without a single user-facing revision convention. Git SHA names an immutable commit, manifest_version is task-state concurrency/version metadata, controller revision is run-local, and protocol version is compatibility semantics. Treating any one of them as the user-facing version leaks implementation detail and causes confusion.
learned_constraints: Subversion assigns a monotonically increasing repository-wide natural-number revision to each accepted commit; this makes rN convenient as a human changeset/tree reference but depends on a centralized repository model.
Git does not natively provide an SVN-style repository-global integer revision; immutable commit object identity remains the technical source of truth.
Git tags are intended to mark important points such as releases, so tagging every checkpoint would create unnecessary ref clutter.
git describe can produce a tag + commit-count + abbreviated hash engineering identifier, but it depends on tag history and is not the right user-facing durable-task state version.
Calendar Versioning is useful when time itself communicates meaningful release context, but a date alone does not distinguish multiple durable checkpoints on the same day.

alternatives.reason: Requires a new mutable daily counter, reset rules, timezone policy and cross-writer coordination. That creates exactly the extra authority/conflict surface the user wants to avoid.
Duplicates commit identity and clutters refs; tags should remain optional stable-release markers.
Exact and immutable but poor for human chronology and not what the user is asking for.
Derive one display label from already-authoritative fields: scope code + persisted calendar date + existing monotonic manifest/owner version. No new counter, no new authority, no Git-history scan.

accepted_design.name: Human Durable Revision
accepted_design.date_source: calendar date of the authoritative persisted updated_at/persisted_at value as encoded; do not silently timezone-convert it for label generation
accepted_design.sequence_source: existing authoritative manifest_version or owner-equivalent monotonic durable version

receipt_semantics.COMMITTED: show the newly persisted Human Durable Revision
receipt_semantics.NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE: show the same last persisted Human Durable Revision and explicitly say unchanged
receipt_semantics.COMMIT_FAILED: do not mint a new revision; show the last verified persisted revision if known
receipt_semantics.STALE_WRITER: do not mint a new revision; current writer lost authority
receipt_semantics.resume: show the pre-takeover persisted Human Durable Revision before lease mutation

cross_agent_decision: This is not maintenance-only. It is a generic user-facing durable-state presentation convention. Pilot and validate it in Universal first. Future owner adoption must derive from each owner's existing monotonic durable version and stable scope code; no global cross-repo counter and no copied owner list.

complexity_budget.implementation: extend existing progress/version policies plus one small deterministic formatting helper and focused tests

assurance_ceiling: This improves human revision observability and prevents version-namespace confusion. It does not replace Git identity, protocol compatibility, business owner versions, or independent quality evidence.
